title: Capacity Evidence Playbook and Error-Budget Retrospective Matrix
author: Morgan Lee
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a practical, repeatable approach to capture high-quality evidence during model-serving and inference incidents, run structured error-budget retrospectives, and convert retrospective outcomes into SLO-grounded capacity commitments. It combines quick operational checklists for on-call, a forensic evidence matrix for post-incident analysis, and a capacity-forecasting workflow so that action items have measurable effects on reliability.

Audience: SREs, on-call engineers for model-serving, platform owners, and product stakeholders responsible for SLOs and capacity planning.

Goals
- Ensure on-call captures the minimal viable evidence set for forensic analysis without blocking recovery.
- Standardize the retrospective matrix so action items link to a capacity change, experiment, or monitoring improvement.
- Provide a clear SLO→error-budget→capacity pipeline (what to do when error budget is exhausted or at risk).

Scope
- Applies to model-serving clusters (hosted + dedicated), the inference routing layer, caching/KV subsystems, and autoscaling controllers.
- Excludes lower-level hardware failures that are handled by infra on-call except where they directly impact SLOs for serving.

Quick definitions (for this doc)
- SLO (Availability): percentage of requests served within latency target and without catastrophic error.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO, consumption measured per rolling 30-day window unless otherwise specified.
- Capacity signal: telemetry that directly correlates with available serving capacity (GPU utilization by slice, queueing latency p95/p99 by tenant, token-generation throughput).

Roles and ownership
- Incident commander (IC): leads triage, ensures evidence collection steps are running.
- Data collector (on-call or runbook automation): executes CLI captures and snapshotting.
- Forensics owner (SRE engineer): ties evidence to retrospective matrix and writes the analysis.
- Capacity owner (platform capacity manager): translates actions into bookings, reservations, or autoscale policy changes.

SLOs and thresholds (examples)
| SLO name | Target | Measurement window | Critical thresholds (action) |
|----------|--------|--------------------|----------------------------|
| Inference success-rate | 99.90% | 30d rolling | < 99.70% -> start error-budget review; < 99.50% -> declare degraded and invoke capacity hedges |
| p95 generation latency (small seq) | 250ms | 7d rolling | > 300ms sustained 15m -> paging and investigate batching/queueing |
| Embedding throughput (per-node) | 1200 reqs/s | 7d rolling | sustained >85% node GPU utilization -> capacity forecast alert |

Note: These are examples. Service owners must publish explicit SLO definitions in the SLO registry and link to that page in the retrospective.

Minimal evidence checklist (Incident-time) — capture these ASAP
1) Short summary (1–3 lines) in the incident timeline with timestamps and observed customer impact.
2) Stack traces / application logs: capture 15 minutes before, during, and 30 minutes after the first error spike. Command: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-serving --since=45m --tail=1000 > /tmp/logs-incident-$(date +%s).log
3) Telemetry snapshots: pull p95/p99 latency, request rate, queue length, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate for impacted clusters. Example Prometheus queries saved as CSV via curl to TSDB read API.
4) Routing and rollout state: capture current routing table, model variant pinned, and rollout policy. Example: curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing?env=prod > /tmp/routing.json
5) Autoscaler and resource events: kubectl describe hpa <name> and cloud autoscaler events (GCP/AWS) for last 60m.
6) Cache/KV state dumps (if safe): trigger the internal cache-dump job with ttl-tagging to limit size. Note: Only do when safe — never block critical recovery flows.
7) Reproduction harness (if feasible): stash the ingestion request that triggered the spike (anonymize PII) and a minimal reproduction script in a sandboxed environment.
8) Snapshot of feature-flag and rollout config (hash + change history).

Evidence capture commands (examples)
- Capture Prometheus metrics to CSV: curl -s -G 'https://prometheus.api.internal/api/v1/query_range' --data-urlencode 'query=sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (service)' --data-urlencode 'start=<ts>' --data-urlencode 'end=<ts>' --data-urlencode 'step=15' > /tmp/metrics.csv
- Export node-level GPU utilization (Fleet metrics API): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://fleet.api.internal/v1/gpu?start=<ts>&end=<ts> > /tmp/gpu.json
- Create incident evidence bundle (automation): /usr/local/bin/incident-bundle --service inference --since 45m --out /tmp/incident-bundle-$(date +%s).tgz

Forensics evidence matrix (post-incident)
- Use this structured table during the retrospective. Capture one row per observed failure mode. Columns are textual and should be completed verbosely.
Columns: Issue ID | Symptom & customer impact | Scope (# tenants / % requests) | Capacity signal(s) seen | Key evidence artifacts (filenames, dashboards) | Probable root cause | Immediate mitigations taken | Proposed capacity or policy commitment | Owner | Due date | Test to validate fix

Example row (text):
- Issue ID: 2024-09-inference-throttle-01
- Symptom: sudden p99 tail latency increase, 45 minutes of 5–10% client errors for the embeddings endpoint.
- Scope: single region, 3 tenants impacted, 3% of total requests.
- Capacity signals: GPU utilization for node-pool-a jumped from 55% to 98% (15m), request queue length rose 8x, autoscaler failed to add nodes due to quota error.
- Artifacts: /tmp/metrics.csv, /tmp/logs-incident-169XYZ.log, dashboard "embeddings/latency/p99", GCP events export /tmp/gce-events.json.
- Probable root cause: resource quota exhausted + conservative autoscaler cooldown window.
- Immediate mitigations: rolled back a tenant heavyweight rollout, manually increased node pool by 2 GPUs.
- Commitment: update autoscaler policy to reduce cooldown from 300s to 90s for embeddings service and create reserved capacity of 10 GPUs for peak windows.
- Owner: Capacity Team (Priya N.)
- Due date: 2024-11-01
- Test: scheduled synthetic traffic test reproducing peak and verifying autoscale triggers in staging.

Retrospective cadence and deliverables
- Trigger: When rolling 30-day error budget burn exceeds warning threshold (50% of budget) or when any incident has >2hr customer impact.
- Cadence: Error-budget retros every 2 weeks; full capacity-commitment reviews monthly.
- Deliverables per retrospective: completed evidence matrix, prioritized action item list with owners and due dates, updated SLO/alert rules if needed, simulation plan for capacity commit verification.

Converting retro outcomes into capacity commitments (workflow)
1) Prioritize actions by risk and SLO impact (High/Medium/Low). 2) For capacity actions (e.g., reserved GPUs, burst pool adjustments), capacity owner creates a capacity ticket with: justification (link to evidence matrix), cost estimate, and rollback plan. 3) Finance should be CC'd for commitments >$5k/month. 4) For autoscaler/tuning changes, create a canary and test plan in staging and schedule controlled rollout with rollback gates. 5) Record the commitment in the capacity ledger (internal sheet) and attach measurement criteria (how we will measure success after 30 days).

Capacity forecasting procedure (monthly)
Inputs required:
- 30-day rolling request volume and growth rate by tenant
- Model mix (average tokens per request per model variant)
- Recent p95/p99 latency trends
- Known upcoming product events (marketing / customer launches)
- Current reservations and committed capacity

Steps:
1) Pull telemetry export for request volume and tokens per request by model variant (PromQL or internal API).
2) Compute tokens-per-GPU throughput baseline from the last 14 days of controlled experiments.
3) Estimate required GPUs for a 95th percentile traffic estimate using safety factor (default 25%).
4) Produce a ticket with proposed reservations or autoscaler policy changes and attach the evidence (CSV exports + calculation sheet).
5) Capacity review meeting: capacity owner presents the forecast; SRE leadership signs off or requests further experiments.

Sample capacity calculation table (as text)
| Tenant | 95th req/s | avg tokens/req | tokens/s | tokens/s per GPU | GPUs required | safety factor | GPUs committed |
| AcmeCorp | 120 | 400 | 48,000 | 24,000 | 2.0 | 4 | 5 |
| BetaApp  | 45  | 1200| 54,000 | 24,000 | 2.0 | 3 | 3 |

Operational tooling integrations
- Incident-bundle: wraps common telemetry grabs and uploads to evidence S3. Usage: incident-bundle --service embeddings --since 60m --upload s3://evidence-bucket/incidents/2024-09-12-embeddings.tgz
- capacity-forecast CLI: ./capacity-forecast generate --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-01-31 --service inference --out forecast-jan-2025.csv
- Alert rule example (Prometheus-style snippet):
  ALERT HighClusterGPUUtilization
  IF avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization{service="embeddings"}[15m]) > 0.85
  FOR 15m
  LABELS { severity = "page", owner = "capacity-team" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary = "GPU utilization >85% for 15m", runbook = "/confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/capacity-evidence-playbook-and-retro-matrix-2024" }

Validation and verification
- Every capacity commitment must have a verification plan: synthetic canary traffic profile, success criteria (SLO non-regression for 30d), and a rollback gate.
- Example verification test: 30-minute synthetic workload ramp to 120% of 95th traffic while verifying p95 latency < target and autoscaler adds <= expected nodes.

Templates (postmortem action item ticket description)
Title: [Action] Reserve X GPUs for <service> to reduce autoscale latency
Description: Evidence: link to matrix row 2024-09-inference-throttle-01; Root cause: quota exhaustion + long cooldown; Proposed action: reserve 10 GPUs in region-prod-a from 2024-11-01; Cost estimate: $Y/month; Verification: synthetic canary scheduled 2024-11-05; Owner: Priya N.; Due: 2024-11-01

Governance and escalation
- If a retrospective proposes >$10k/month recurring capacity, Ops leadership must approve and Finance should be looped in.
- If SLO regression is not resolved within the retro due date, escalate to platform leadership and require a remediation plan within 5 business days.

Privacy and security notes
- Evidence bundles must be scrubbed for PII before sharing outside SRE. Use the incident-bundle --scrub flag.
- Sensitive customer data captured during an incident must be stored with restricted access and a 90-day retention unless legal requires longer.

Related resources
- SLO registry page (link required by service owners).
- Autoscaler runbook and HPA tuning guide.
- Incident evidence automation repo: git@internal:redwood/incident-tools.git

Appendix: quick-check triage checklist (one page)
1) Notify IC and set timeline. 2) Capture minimal evidence checklist (logs, metrics, routing). 3) Apply immediate mitigations to restore SLO if safe. 4) Create incident ticket and attach raw evidence. 5) After service stable, start retrospective within 3 business days.

Change history
- 2024-09-12 (Morgan Lee): created initial draft and quick-check checklist.
- 2024-11-04 (Morgan Lee): added example evidence matrix row and capacity calculation sample.
